package_info.package_versions: N/A (single malware suite, not versioned as a package)
package_info.why_malicious: HiddenWasp is a fully developed Linux malware suite containing a trojan, rootkit, and deployment script, designed for remote control of infected systems. It enables attackers to download and execute code, upload files, and perform arbitrary commands, using advanced evasion techniques to avoid detection.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The trojan component receives remote commands, downloads and executes code, uploads files, and performs arbitrary shell commands on the infected system.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the trojan listens for remote commands, downloads and executes additional code, uploads files from the system, and executes arbitrary shell commands, enabling full remote control of the infected host.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior provides an attacker with persistent, interactive remote access and control, which is a hallmark of backdoor malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Linux binaries do not open remote command channels or allow arbitrary code execution from remote sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools (RATs) in enterprise environments, but these are installed with user consent and proper authentication.
key_indicators: Ability to download and execute arbitrary code
File upload from victim to attacker

execution_context.file_location: rootkit module (kernel module or LD_PRELOAD library)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The rootkit component hides files, processes, and network connections associated with the malware, preventing detection by system administrators and security tools.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the rootkit intercepts system calls to hide the presence of malware files, processes, and network activity, enabling stealthy persistence on the infected system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Rootkits are designed to conceal malicious activity and maintain persistence, which is inherently suspicious and malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not attempt to hide its files, processes, or network connections from system monitoring tools.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging or anti-cheat software may use similar techniques, but with user awareness and consent.
key_indicators: Hiding of files, processes, or network ports

execution_context.file_location: initial deployment script (bash or shell script)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The deployment script downloads the trojan and rootkit components, installs them on the system, and ensures persistence by modifying system startup scripts or services.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During initial infection, the script downloads malware components, installs them, and modifies system startup routines to ensure the malware persists across reboots.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated download and installation of malware components, along with persistence mechanisms, are classic signs of malicious installation scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installation scripts do not fetch and install unauthorized binaries or modify system startup for persistence without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System management scripts may automate software deployment, but with user approval and from trusted sources.
key_indicators: Modifies /etc/rc.local, systemd, or init scripts for persistence

attack_chain.action: Initial deployment script downloads and installs the trojan and rootkit components, and sets up persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware components are installed and persist on the system.

attack_chain.action: Rootkit component activates to hide the presence of the malware and its activity.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware remains undetected by system administrators and security tools.

attack_chain.action: Trojan component establishes remote command and control, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands, download/upload files, and maintain full remote access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves full remote control and can perform post-exploitation activities.

behavioral_signatures: Installation of unauthorized kernel modules or LD_PRELOAD libraries
Processes that hide themselves or associated files from system monitoring tools
Unusual outbound network connections from non-standard processes
Persistence mechanisms modifying system startup scripts or services
file_indicators: Unknown ELF binaries in /tmp, /var/tmp, or user home directories
Suspicious kernel modules or shared libraries loaded at runtime
Modified /etc/rc.local, systemd service files, or crontab entries
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 IP addresses or domains (as per IOCs)
Unusual traffic patterns from non-standard system processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized kernel modules, hidden processes, and modifications to system startup scripts. Use file integrity monitoring to detect new or modified binaries in sensitive locations. Analyze outbound network connections for links to known C2 infrastructure. Employ YARA rules and threat intelligence IOCs to identify known HiddenWasp components.
